title: Coordinate reversal is an involution on subsets
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and for a subset $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\overline{S} = \{\, i : (n-1) - i \in S \,\}$ be the subset obtained by reversing the coordinate order. Then applying this reversal twice returns the original set: $\overline{\overline{S}} = S$ for every $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
S is an arbitrary subset of Fin n
replaced: Reversing a coordinate set twice recovers it.
